relevance_note: Narrative review that tabulates previously published TNFAIP3-variant patients row by row and describes many of them individually, e.g. 'This mutation was observed in an 11-year-old child with recurrent lower back pain and recurrent ulcers.'
method_note: Review (no new patients); everyone is a previously published person with source_reference_in_review taken from the table Reference column or the bracketed citation in the text. Tables 1-3 have no patient label column, so table people are 'Table n row k'. The 66 table rows were parsed by a short script and each transcribed cell was checked against the table; all values, features and checklist statuses were chosen by reading. Linking table rows to text: a table row with a single age of onset was treated as one person (the index case) and merged with the text's description of the patient with the same variant and same reference number. Rows whose onset cell lists several ages/ranges (Table 2 rows 5, 20, 34, 37, 38, 41, 44, 45: Arg87Ter [35], Phe224Ser fs*4 [48], Cys478Ter [54], Lys564Ter [34], His577Alafs*95 [57], Thr604Argfs*93 [48], Glu730Ser fs*83 [34], Gln737Ser fs*79 [62]) and Table 2 row 7 (Lys91Ter [36,37], whose symptom cell mixes features the text assigns to different relatives) were treated as family summaries: no row-person was created and their cells were not attributed; people described individually in the text got 'ref [..] patient' labels. Table 2 row 41 Thr604Argfs*93 cites [48] but the text proband cites [49]; the text proband is 'ref [49] patient'. The 119 kb microdeletion patient in the text cites [25,27] but resembles Table 1 row 6 ([28]: microdeletion, IBD) and partly row 1 ([25]); kept as a separate person 'ref [25,27] patient' (possible duplicate; text says 'no additional developmental delay' whereas Table 1 row 6 lists developmental delay). Pro268Leufs*19: table cites [49], text cites [73]; linked by variant and MEFV detail; both references recorded. Leu303fs*26 [34]: text describes two patients; Table 2 row 26 matches 'one of them' (abdominal pain, diarrhea, colon inflammation); the other is 'ref [34] patient'. Group statements ('They did not have fever or genital ulcers...', 'Both of them...') applied to both as inferred from group statement. Contradictions between table and text (table value used for age_at_onset; text onset kept in feature onsets): Table 2 row 3 onset 11 years vs 'before her first year of age'; row 9 2 years vs 'at the age of 3 months'; row 12 2 years vs 'since his first year of age'; row 16 3 years vs 'in his teenage years'; row 40 32 vs symptoms 'at the age of 36'; Table 3 row 1 29 vs 'at the age of 15'; Table 3 row 4 13 years vs '15 months of age' (row content also partly resembles the father); Table 3 row 6 4 years vs 'teenage years' and family history 'De novo' vs affected relatives; Table 3 row 2 family history Positive vs 'No other affected family members'; Table 2 row 35 family history Positive vs 'None of his relatives presented with similar disease phenotypes'; Table 2 row 10 family history NA vs text positive; Table 3 row 10 NA vs mother positive. Within-person contradiction: Table 2 row 1 'arthritis' and 'improved her joint symptoms' vs 'There were no joint issues' -> both feature rows emitted, checklist arthritis left not reported. Table 2 row 18 table 'positive autoantibodies' vs text 'negative autoantibodies ... disappeared' (garbled sentence; table value used). Bare numbers in Age of Onset ('10', '5', '4', '29', '32') were converted to years. 'de novo' statements (Table 1 row 5, Table 2 rows 21 and 27, Table 3 row 6) give no parental testing, so inheritance is not reported; only Glu192Lys (father carries it) and Met476Ile (mother positive) have inheritance. Variant type: Table 1 caption ('Large deletions') and Table 3 caption ('Missense mutations') used as named groups; Table 2 caption lists several classes, so Table 2 types come only from text ('splice site mutation', 'nonsense mutation'). Zygosity not reported for anyone (only general statements about heterozygous mutations). Functional evidence: Zhou et al. sentence (Phe224fs, Leu227Ter, Arg271Ter, Tyr306Ter, Pro268Leu fs19, Thr604Argfs93) attached to every person carrying one of these exact variants; Schwarz et al. to Thr604Argfs93 and Leu626Valfs*45; Rajamaki to Lys91Ter; His577Alafs*95 chemokine statement to the His577 family. His577Ala fs*95 family: mother and three children included with features from 'All affected members experienced...' (inferred from group statement); variant tied at family level ('reported in an Italian family, where the mother and three children...'). Relatives included when described in relation to an in-scope person with a sex-defining relation or a feature; carriers only where stated (father of Table 3 row 3, mother of Table 3 row 10, sister of ref [54] patient). Not given rows: group-only relatives without a count or identity ('Other relatives' of Table 2 row 2, 'Other affected relatives' of Lys91Ter, 'The daughters of the proband' of Pro268Leufs*19, 'The patient's children' of His636fs*1, Arg87Ter family apart from the one member whose treatment is described, asymptomatic carriers of Ile310Thr/Gln709Arg, 'Some relatives' of Cys243Tyr); parents of Table 2 row 19 (pituitary macroadenoma, Mediterranean anemia: not HA20 features, not tested). Passing mentions 'Glu187Ter and Phe224Serfs*4 ... proliferative glomerulonephritis and membranous lupus nephritis, respectively [8,44]' and 'p.Ala434Ter (c.1300_1301delinsTA) [69]' were not made into new people because they probably restate people already extracted and cannot be tied to one. Checklist conventions: plain 'fever' is not marked recurrent fever (only recurrent/periodic/intermittent/episodic statements); 'oral/genital ulcers' and 'oral/perianal ulcers' are ambiguous and left not reported for the specific ulcer items; anemia/thrombocytopenia/hemolytic anemia count as autoimmune cytopenia only when called autoimmune or immune (Table 2 row 35 'autoimmune-related symptoms ... cytopenia, hepatitis' counted for cytopenia and autoimmune hepatitis; its 'diabetes' not counted as type 1); pericardial effusion and ascites not counted as serositis; joint effusion/swelling alone not counted as arthritis; vitiligo/ecchymosis not counted as skin lesions; negations of a narrower item (uveitis, polyarthritis, lymphadenopathy, ulcers vs GI ulcers or inflammation) do not exclude the broader checklist item. No transcripts are printed anywhere in the paper.
